references.text: God forbade the people from approaching Mount Sinai; only Moses was allowed to come near to the Lord.
Moses approached alone into the thick darkness where God was, while the people stood at a distance.
Moses was again commanded to go up to the Lord alone, with no one else accompanying him.
The Lord called Moses up to the top of Mount Sinai, a special access that only Moses had.
Moses stood between the Lord and the people because they were afraid of the fire and did not go up on the mountain.
Reference to the awe-inspiring scene at Sinai where the people could not approach, in contrast to the grace of the new covenant.
Moses' role as mediator between God and the people during the giving of the law at Sinai.
The Lord spoke with Moses face to face, like a friend, a unique closeness that only Moses had.
Moses' unique position among the prophets; he spoke with God directly and not through visions or dreams.
A direct parallel in the same event confirming God's requirement for boundaries at Sinai.
Warning about the consequences of breaking the boundaries toward God's holy presence.
Moses confirms that the restriction is a fulfillment of God's earlier command to consecrate the mountain.
